about: A set of extra Git commands for everyday chores, like squashing branches and summing up a repo.

prs.title: Squash leaves unfinished edits alone
prs.broken: git squash also swept in any edited file you had not staged, putting half-done work into the commit.
prs.changed: It now commits only what is staged.
prs.matters: Work in progress stays out of the squashed commit.

prs.title: merge-into no longer applies an old stash
prs.broken: With only untracked files present, merge-into stashed nothing and then popped an older, unrelated stash onto the branch.
prs.changed: It now stashes only when there are tracked changes to save.
prs.matters: Saved work in the stash stays where it was.

prs.title: effort and summary count files with non-ASCII names
prs.broken: git effort skipped files with accented or other non-ASCII names, and git summary counted no lines for them.
prs.changed: Both now read file names as they are instead of git's quoted form.
prs.matters: Projects with non-English file names get full stats.

prs.title: Merging a repo into the current folder keeps dotfiles
prs.broken: Merging another repository into the current folder left out its hidden files, and could apply an old saved change by mistake.
prs.changed: Hidden files are now included, and only the change saved during the merge is restored.
prs.matters: Merged repositories arrive complete, without surprise edits.
